search_scope_note: This result records what was recovered in the searched public official/archive surfaces. NOT_FOUND and NOT_RECOVERED are not claims that a record never existed, is destroyed, remains classified, or is concealed.

D0_CONTEMPORANEOUS_PRIMARY_REPORT.details: NARA holds Project Blue Book case files/OSI records. Public archive reproductions and later government-republished analysis identify a same-day 745th ACWRON/Duncanville TWX, E.T. Piwetz wing-intelligence summary and Major Lewis Chase Airborne Observer Data Sheet. These preserve timed reports and instrument descriptions but are reports, not raw sensor streams.

D1_RAW_SENSOR_RECORD.details: No authenticated continuous ALA-6/APR-9/ALA-5 recording, radar-scope film/tape, or raw ground-radar plot was recovered in the searched official public web surfaces.

D2_SENSOR_CALIBRATION_CONFIGURATION.details: Surviving documents/analyses describe receiver type, reported signal frequency/pulse characteristics and relative bearings. They do not supply a calibration package sufficient to turn all reported contacts into error-bounded physical coordinates.

D3_PLATFORM_NAVIGATION_TIMEBASE.details: Typed chronology contains times, locations/headings and aircraft state at selected points, but no complete synchronized navigation/attitude stream was recovered.

D4_CROSS_SENSOR_SYNCHRONIZATION.details: The case file/reconstructions report visual, ELINT and ground-radar correlations. Publicly recovered material does not provide common-time raw recordings from the channels.

D5_ENVIRONMENT_TRAFFIC_CONTROLS.details: Competing radar-source/aircraft/propagation hypotheses have been discussed historically, but R2 did not recover a complete contemporaneous environment/traffic dataset adequate to close them quantitatively.

nonofficial_discovery_mirrors_not_promot: Public reproductions of the Project Blue Book RB-47 case file were used only to locate document names/content boundaries; they are not treated as a substitute for an official NARA byte-level case-file bind.

D0_CONTEMPORANEOUS_PRIMARY_REPORT.details: DoD authenticated the November 2004 Navy video. Navy deck logs for the Nimitz period have been FOIA-recovered. Public official evidence does not include a contemporaneous complete incident investigation binding every channel.

D1_RAW_SENSOR_RECORD.details: The Navy/DoD FLIR1 video is an authentic sensor record. R2 did not recover USS Princeton AN/SPY-1 raw returns, E-2C AN/APS-145 returns, APG-73 raw radar data, air-defense-net audio, or equivalent continuous sensor tracks. A FY2023 Navy FOIA request explicitly seeking Princeton radar returns, E-2C radar returns, air-defense audio, sonar data and official exercise/UAP reports was closed as Full Denial - No Records Located.

D2_SENSOR_CALIBRATION_CONFIGURATION.details: The released targeting-pod video contains sensor symbology/mode information, but no public complete calibration/range solution sufficient to derive extraordinary target kinematics independently.

D3_PLATFORM_NAVIGATION_TIMEBASE.details: Public material does not bind a full synchronized platform navigation/attitude stream to the video and reported ship/E-2 radar tracks.

D4_CROSS_SENSOR_SYNCHRONIZATION.details: No public continuous common-time raw track binds the multi-day Princeton radar reports, Fravor/Dietrich visual encounter, E-2 channel and later FLIR1 target as one continuous object.

D5_ENVIRONMENT_TRAFFIC_CONTROLS.details: Training-area context and some deck/flight information are public, but not a complete synchronized airspace/environment denominator for the claimed target trajectory.

official_foia_findings: NAVAIR internal FOIA correspondence in 2020 states that N2N6/ONI/NAVAIR were familiar with the released videos, but there was not a formal custody process for accompanying transfer documents and officials expected few/no responsive records in that search context.

FY2023 Department of the Navy FOIA log entry DON-NAVY-2023-012523 requested USS Princeton radar returns, E-2C radar returns, air-defense audio, USS Louisville sonar data and official reports for the November 2004 Nimitz CSG exercise; disposition: Full Denial - No Records Located.
Sworn 2023 congressional testimony by David Fravor states the relevant radar tape was never released and its whereabouts were unknown to him.

D0_CONTEMPORANEOUS_PRIMARY_REPORT.details: DIA Electronic Reading Room publishes the DoD/JCS message forwarding the 19 September 1976 Tehran incident report. It records visual observations, reported F-4 instrumentation/communications failures and a second F-4 radar lock.

D1_RAW_SENSOR_RECORD.details: No public official F-4 radar tape/scope recording, ground-radar raw log, weapon-system telemetry or avionics data stream was found in the searched DIA/NARA official public surfaces.

D2_SENSOR_CALIBRATION_CONFIGURATION.details: The message reports lock range 27 NM, closure 150 NMPH, approximate maintained range 25 NM and return-size comparison, but supplies no radar mode/calibration/error model from which to reconstruct uncertainty.

D3_PLATFORM_NAVIGATION_TIMEBASE.details: Takeoff and event times/directions are narrated; no complete synchronized aircraft navigation/attitude stream was recovered.

D4_CROSS_SENSOR_SYNCHRONIZATION.details: The primary message correlates visual/radar/system effects in a common story, but R2 did not recover independent raw channel recordings on a common timebase.

D5_ENVIRONMENT_TRAFFIC_CONTROLS.details: The primary message notes no helicopters airborne and contact with Mehrabad Tower, but a full air-traffic/weather/astronomy/radar-propagation control dataset was not recovered.

targets.foia_search_context: DIA FOIA logs show multiple public requests concerning the 19 September 1976 F-4 interception. The searched electronic reading room surfaced the contemporaneous message but not geometry-enabling sensor records.

cross_case_result.reason: Every target preserves some serious evidence, but none supplies the public synchronized raw measurements plus calibration/geometry needed to calculate the extraordinary-performance claims with defensible uncertainty.

new_archival_context.NARA_RG615_state_2026_09_28: NARA's rolling UAP collection publicly lists transfers from FAA, NRC, ODNI, OSD, NSA, State, FBI, Air Force and CBP. This creates a future discovery surface, but R2 did not find a geometry-enabling top-three dataset in the currently indexed public material.
new_archival_context.future_rule: A newly transferred official record may reopen only the corresponding data-class gate; it does not retroactively validate prior kinematic estimates.

scientific_verdict: R2 FAILS TO RECOVER THE MISSING MEASUREMENT LAYER. THE TOP THREE REMAIN LEGITIMATE DOCUMENTARY RESIDUALS OF DIFFERENT STRENGTH, BUT NONE IS CURRENTLY A PUBLICLY REPRODUCIBLE PHYSICAL ANOMALY.

next_gate.recommended_action: Stop broad UAP browsing. Target only named archival objects whose recovery would change G3: RB-47 case-file primary bytes/raw radar or ELINT media; Nimitz Princeton/E-2/APG-73 raw records or custody disposition; Tehran F-4/ground-radar/maintenance records.
do_not_accept: derived acceleration estimates whose range/time assumptions are not primary measurements
next_gate.success_condition: At least one recovered official primary artifact changes D1-D4 from missing/partial to geometry-enabling.

canonical_seal: R1 ASKED WHICH STORIES SURVIVE. R2 ASKED WHETHER THE MEASUREMENTS SURVIVE. THE STORIES DID; THE GEOMETRY-ENABLING RAW DATA DID NOT ARRIVE.
